title: Neena Rani v. State of U.P.
coram: Ferdino Inacio Rebello, C.J. and Vineet Saran, J.
disposition: Connection directed on Annexure 4.2 bond; third-party recall rejected.
headnote: On the licensee's statement that supply would be given if the applicant furnished a bond in terms of Annexure 4.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ was disposed of with a direction to release the connection within two weeks of a properly formatted bond. A later recall by a non-party claiming possession was refused: a pending title suit was left to the civil court, and the connection direction conferred no proprietary right on the consumer.
facts: Neena Rani petitioned the Allahabad High Court for an electricity connection from the Power Corporation. After two listings for instructions, counsel for the respondents stated that a connection would be given if she furnished a bond in terms of Annexure 4.2 of the Electricity Supply Code; she was willing. A non-party later applied to recall the disposal, claiming she was in possession and alleging connivance. She relied on a pending title suit against original allottee Ugrasen Jain, through whom the petitioner claimed ownership.

holding_units.topic: indemnity bond as condition of new connection
holding_units.holding: On the licensee's statement, a new connection shall be released within two weeks of the applicant furnishing a bond in the proper format under Annexure 4.2 of the Supply Code. A later recall by a non-party claiming possession was refused: a pending title suit against the original allottee was not decided, and the connection direction did not itself confer any right on the consumer.

not_decided.point: Title to and possession of the premises
not_decided.note: Applicant's title suit against original allottee Ugrasen Jain left to the civil court; the connection order confers no proprietary right.
